brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.

requirements.evidence: Four level-0 hexagonal cells in a cluster: pieces at 0,0, 1,0, 0,1 and 1,-1 (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full).

requirements.requirement: Each cell with a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each of the four cells holds a hex-bin-full-drain bin (draining bin family): bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:0,1,0 and bin:1,-1,0, all '~hex-bin-full-drain'.

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray (shown in use for seedlings)
requirements.evidence: All four draining bins were filled with soil and planted via fill_and_plant (prop:1–prop:4); the from-above look (polar 10) confirms all four plants are visible, and check_build reports no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL warnings.

finish.summary: A 4-cell seed-starting tray: four full hexagonal bases in a 2×2-style cluster, each holding a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain). Open faces were capped and joints locked per house rules. Each bin was filled with soil and planted with a seedling so the tray reads as in-use for seed starting; check_build passes with mesh clear and no warnings.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
